title: Sessions

stateHint.active: Working now — events within the expected cadence.
stateHint.silent_evasion: Gone silent inside its expected cadence — a signal worth your eye, not an error.

evasionBanner: This session went silent within its expected cadence. The engine flags it as a possible evasion — review the timeline.

detail.title: Session
detail.minimalData: Only metadata is shown. By design the engine never carries SQL, payloads or secrets here (minimal-data).

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.subtitle: Reconstructed ingest order — newest events appear as they arrive.
timeline.emptyHint: As the session emits tool, MCP, cost and finding events, they appear here.

empty.title: No sessions yet
empty.description: Sessions you start, and the ones Olivares finds, appear here.

filtered.title: No sessions match these filters
filtered.description: Clear the filters to show your sessions.

forbidden.title: Sessions not authorized
forbidden.description: Your role does not include permission to view live sessions.

partial.noLiveRead: Observed sessions are not shown: your role does not include sessions:live:read. The launched ones below are the part that could be read, not the whole picture.
partial.noRunRead: Launched sessions are not shown: your role does not include sessions:run:read. A session below reading as discovered may still have been launched by Olivares — this list could not check.
partial.truncated: This is the most recent page, not the whole estate. Origin here is joined over what is loaded, so a session whose run has scrolled off can read as discovered; open a session to have the engine answer for it.
partial.runLookupFailed: The launched half could not be read: the run lookup failed. Rows below show what the observed half returned; origin is reported as not read rather than guessed.
partial.liveLookupFailed: The observed half could not be read: the live lookup failed. Rows below are the launched ones; the telemetry columns are empty because nothing could be read, not because there is none.
partial.noProfileRead: Provider profile names are not shown: your role does not include sessions:profile:read. The Instance column carries each row's profile reference instead.
partial.profileLookupFailed: Provider profile names could not be read: the profile lookup failed. The Instance column carries each row's profile reference instead.

provenance.launchedExplain: A launch record links this session to Olivares: it started this session. What can be done with it now is below — a launch is not the same as a live process.
provenance.discoveredExplain: No launch record links this session, so as far as this plane can prove, Olivares did not start it. It can be read and audited, not steered.
provenance.unknownExplain: Whether Olivares launched this session could not be checked — no permission for sessions:run:read, or the lookup failed. This is “not read”, not “not launched”.

control.title: What can be done with it
control.fullExplain: Olivares holds the process and bridges its I/O: it can be watched, driven and stopped.
control.lifecycleExplain: Start and stop, nothing in between: either Olivares holds the process but not its I/O, or the process is stopped and can be resumed.
control.observeExplain: Olivares holds no process for this session. It can be read and audited; stopping it is not something this plane can do.
control.unknownExplain: The operate half was not read (sessions:run:read), so this is what is visible from the observed half alone.

cap.watch: Watch its live telemetry and timeline
cap.attach: See its I/O as it happens

reason.no-run: no process: Olivares did not launch this session
reason.no-observation: nothing observed for this session yet
reason.transport: its I/O is relayed to Anthropic’s cloud, so Olivares cannot show or drive it
reason.state: not in a state that allows it
reason.permission: your role does not include it

actions.cleanupHint: Closes the run and releases its resume handle, so it can no longer be resumed. The lifecycle ledger is kept.
actions.deleteHint: Removes the session. It can no longer be continued; its lifecycle events stay in the audit log.

postureValue.enforced: Enforced — its tool calls are policed in line
postureValue.observed: Observed — its tool calls are recorded, not policed

card.unclaimed: Activity seen from a session holding no live claim. The engine reports it; it is not the same signal as a possible evasion.
card.relayedIO: Its I/O is relayed to Anthropic’s cloud, so Olivares cannot show it here. Lifecycle control still applies.
card.observedNotRead: The observed half was not read: your role does not include sessions:live:read.
card.failureReasonMissing: This session failed. The server did not report a reason.
card.hostIsolationRemedy: Ask the server administrator to allow unprivileged user and network namespaces and Landlock, then start the session again.
card.actionFailed: The action could not be completed.
card.pickRun: Several runs drive this session. Pick one to attach, govern or stop it.

attributionExplain.legacy: Folded from a channel with no registered source: a legacy connector, a pushed collector observation or an old event. It is never assigned a provider instance after the fact.
attributionExplain.observed: Arrived through a source dedicated to this provider profile. That says which configured source delivered it — not that the id inside belongs to a process Olivares launched.
attributionExplain.source: Arrived through a registered source that is not dedicated to any profile: the channel is known, the provider instance is not.
attributionExplain.managed: Written by Olivares' own bridge for a session it launched: the only row that carries a proven canonical session and run.

related.title: Also observed through bound sources
related.explain: These rows share this run's profile and provider session id but arrived through a source, not through the process Olivares holds. They are shown beside the run, never merged into it.

address.retired: The session you had open is closed. Your access to the half it came from changed. Select a row to open a session under your current access.

rail.label: Work rail
rail.noObservation: No telemetry has arrived for this session yet.

narrative.noneDescription: Choose a session in the rail to read what it did, with its evidence beside it.
narrative.notReadTitle: This session could not be read

meter.costTitle: An estimate, not an invoice: the tool's own figure, or the list price of a turn it did not price
meter.planLabel: The plan's usage windows of this session's login

evidence.forbiddenDescription: Your role does not include permission to read session telemetry.
evidence.errorTitle: The evidence could not be read
evidence.errorDescription: The timeline read did not answer. An empty list here would mean the session did nothing, which is a different fact.

context.noneDescription: The scope a session ran under, and the references you need to look it up, appear here.
context.scopeHint: What this session applies to. These are the values it ran under, not the ones selected now. Read-only folders protect file content and directory entries (no write, truncate, create, remove or rename); permissions, ownership, extended attributes and timestamps follow the host's normal permissions.
context.traceHint: The references this session is known by, and what the plane recorded about it.
context.pepOn: Tool calls are policed in line.
context.pepOff: Tool calls are not policed in line.
context.recordOn: Input and output are anchored as evidence.
context.recordOff: Input and output are not recorded.
context.identifiersHint: References to copy. They are not the names on the scope line.
context.wireHint: The raw frame for the selected line. The conversation is the default view.
context.wireEmpty: Select a line in the conversation to see its raw frame.
context.workHint: Recorded for the last launch. Every action checks current authorization.
context.toolMode: Mode as the tool reports it

context.noChanges: Olivares did not start this session, so it has no changes to show.
context.filesUnavailable: This folder is not available to browse.
context.filesNoAccess: Your role cannot browse this folder.
context.filesFailed: The folder could not be read.
